title: Ring universal property of a scalar module telescope
statement: Let C be a preadditive monoidal category whose tensor is additive in each variable, with sequential colimits preserved by tensoring on either side. Let l be a natural number, R,S monoid objects, and i:R→S a monoid morphism. Suppose a colimit of the regular R-module telescope with transitions l times the identity has vertex S restricted along i, and its zeroth leg has underlying map i. If l acts invertibly on S, then for any monoid object B on which l acts invertibly and every monoid morphism a:R→B, there exists a unique monoid morphism b:S→B with i followed by b equal to a. This uses the module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and ring objects of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object].

source.place: Ring universal property of a scalar module telescope

proof.text: The forgetful functor from R-modules to C preserves the given sequential colimit, since tensorLeft R preserves such colimits. Write j_n for its underlying legs. Naturality gives l times j_(n+1) = j_n, and j_0 = i. For any target T with invertible multiplication by l, scalar cancellation and induction show that two maps from S to T agreeing after j_0 agree after every j_n, hence are equal by the underlying colimit property.

Given a:R to B, define k_0=a and k_(n+1)=k_n followed by inverse multiplication by l on B. Scalar cancellation gives l times k_(n+1)=k_n, so these maps form a cocone on the underlying scalar sequence. Its colimit descent b satisfies i followed by b=a. Since i and a preserve the unit, b preserves the unit.

To compare multiplication on S followed by b with tensor(b,b) followed by multiplication on B, apply the zeroth-leg uniqueness argument first to the colimit preserved by tensorRight S, then to that preserved by tensorLeft R. Additivity carries the scalar recurrence to these tensor legs. It remains to compare after tensor(i,i); both sides equal multiplication on R followed by a, since i and a are monoid morphisms and i followed by b=a. Bundle b as a monoid morphism. Zeroth-leg uniqueness also proves uniqueness among all monoid morphisms extending a. The argument uses only the inverse scalar on B, and remains valid for l=0 and zero objects.

proof_origin.place: Ring structure paragraph; underlying scalar telescope descent and zeroth-leg uniqueness after tensoring replace explicit pairwise fraction formulas.

mathlib_searches.query: universal property of localization of a ring object given by a scalar telescope of regular modules
mathlib_searches.verdict: Ordinary modules; no ring-object universal property in an arbitrary preadditive monoidal category.

mathlib_searches.query: colimit of regular module objects along multiplication by a natural number has the universal property of localization as a ring object
mathlib_searches.verdict: The scalar transitions are module maps, not ring maps, so ordinary ring-colimit results do not apply.

mathlib_searches.query: scalar_telescope_ring_universal; ring localization universal; telescope in Mathlib and both project roots
mathlib_searches.results: PadicIntegersInvertEll supplies module telescopes and comparisons with commutative colimit models; RingLocalizationSheafification supplies localization among commutative ring objects. Neither gives the required arbitrary ring-object test property from a module telescope.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Extract precisely the ring-structure argument missing from these APIs.

lean.statement:
theorem scalar_telescope_ring_universal
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory C] [Preadditive C]
    [MonoidalPreadditive C] [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ C]
    [∀ A : C, PreservesColimitsOfShape ℕ (tensorLeft A)]
    [∀ A : C, PreservesColimitsOfShape ℕ (tensorRight A)]
    (l : ℕ) (R S : Mon C) (i : R ⟶ S)
    (ι : Functor.ofSequence (fun _ : ℕ ↦ l • 𝟙 (Mod.regular R.X)) ⟶
      (Functor.const ℕ).obj ((Mod.comap i.hom).obj (Mod.regular S.X)))
    (h0 : (ι.app 0).hom = i.hom)
    (hc : IsColimit (Cocone.mk ((Mod.comap i.hom).obj (Mod.regular S.X)) ι))
    (hi : IsIso (l • 𝟙 S.X)) :
    ∀ (B : Mon C), IsIso (l • 𝟙 B.X) →
      ∀ a : R ⟶ B, ∃! b : S ⟶ B, i ≫ b = a
